intent.raw_query: Eastern Europe city hop Prague + Budapest, $1200, 8 days, September 2026

selected_hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Prague Old Town & Astronomical Clock Tour
experiences.description: Explore the medieval heart of Prague, wandering through Old Town Square and witnessing the iconic Astronomical Clock strike the hour. Dive into centuries of Bohemian history with a self-guided or local-led walking tour through cobblestone streets, Gothic churches, and Baroque palaces.

experiences.name: Budapest Thermal Bath Experience at Széchenyi
experiences.description: Soak in the grandeur of one of Europe's largest thermal bath complexes, built in 1913. Experience the healing mineral waters in stunning Neo-Baroque surroundings, a quintessential Budapest cultural ritual enjoyed by locals and visitors alike — the closest Budapest gets to a spa-resort waterfront escape.

experiences.name: Danube River Evening Cruise
experiences.description: Board a scenic cruise along the Danube River at sunset to witness Budapest's illuminated Parliament, Buda Castle, and Chain Bridge from the water. This waterfront experience offers the closest equivalent to a beachfront atmosphere in landlocked Budapest, with stunning reflections on the river.

experiences.name: Prague & Budapest Local Food Market Crawl
experiences.description: Sample authentic Central European cuisine across both cities — try trdelník and svíčková in Prague's Manifesto Market, then indulge in lángos, chimney cakes, and goulash at Budapest's Great Market Hall. This dual-city food crawl immerses you in local culinary traditions and vibrant market culture.
experiences.location: Manifesto Market (Prague) & Nagy Vásárcsarnok / Great Market Hall (Budapest)

experiences.name: Buda Castle Hill & Fisherman's Bastion Exploration
experiences.description: Climb or take the funicular up to Buda Castle Hill to explore the Royal Palace, Matthias Church, and the fairy-tale turrets of Fisherman's Bastion. Enjoy panoramic views over the Danube and Pest side — a historically rich half-day adventure blending medieval architecture with breathtaking riverside vistas.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use this time to rest on the plane.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Prague Airport, take the affordable Airport Express bus (Line AE) to Náměstí Republiky for ~60 CZK, then walk or take tram to your hotel in Staré Město (Old Town). Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed first stroll through Old Town Square — admire the iconic Astronomical Clock (Orloj), the Church of Our Lady before Týn, and soak in the medieval atmosphere. Entry to the square is free.
day_by_day.evening: Wander across the Charles Bridge at sunset for stunning views of Prague Castle and the Vltava River — completely free and magical at dusk. Explore the Malá Strana (Lesser Town) side briefly before heading back for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Pick up a traditional Czech 'chlebíčky' (open-faced sandwich) or a fresh pastry from a local bakery near Old Town Square for under 80 CZK (~€3).
meals.dinner: Lokál Dlouhááá (Dlouhá 33, Old Town) — a beloved local Czech pub serving authentic svíčková (beef sirloin with cream sauce) and tank-fresh Pilsner Urquell. Budget ~250–350 CZK (~€10–14) per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Focus on orientation and gentle exploration. Get a 24-hour public transport pass (120 CZK) from the airport or any metro station — it covers trams, metro, and buses. Keep jet lag in mind and prioritize rest.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) — the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Purchase the Circuit B ticket (~250 CZK) which covers St. Vitus Cathedral, Old Royal Palace, and St. George's Basilica. Arrive early (by 9:00) to beat the crowds. The walk uphill from Malá Strana is free and scenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through Malá Strana and explore the charming cobblestone streets, Wallenstein Garden (free entry), and Kampa Island along the Vltava riverbank. Cross back over Charles Bridge and visit the Old Town Hall Tower for panoramic views of the city (250 CZK for tower entry).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) from the outside — the synagogues close in the evening but the streets and architecture are free to admire. End the evening with a beer at a local pub near Old Town.

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre-style budget option: grab a fresh croissant and coffee at Café Savoy or a local bakery near the hotel for ~100 CZK.
meals.lunch: Havelský trh (Havelská Market) — a traditional open-air market in Old Town selling grilled sausages (klobása), fresh fruit, and snacks. Lunch for ~100–150 CZK (~€4–6).
meals.dinner: U Fleků (Křemencova 11, Nové Město) — Prague's most famous historic brewery, brewing dark beer since 1499. Try the goulash with bread dumplings. Budget ~300–400 CZK (~€12–16).

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Prague Castle involves a lot of uphill walking and cobblestones. The castle grounds open at 6:00 AM (free to walk through), but buildings open at 9:00 AM. Consider the free Prague Castle grounds walk if budget is very tight.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods — two authentic, less-touristy districts. Walk up to the Žižkov Television Tower (entry ~250 CZK for the observation deck) for 360° views of Prague. Admire the quirky crawling baby sculptures by David Černý on the tower's exterior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum (Národní muzeum) on Wenceslas Square — entry is ~200 CZK and covers Czech natural history and culture. Stroll down Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí), a historic boulevard central to Czech history and the 1989 Velvet Revolution.
day_by_day.evening: Free evening to explore the Nové Město (New Town) area. Check out the Lucerna Passage — a beautiful Art Nouveau arcade with a famous upside-down horse statue by David Černý. Great spot for people-watching and budget shopping.

meals.breakfast: Grab a 'rohlík' (Czech bread roll) with butter and ham from a local potraviny (corner store) — budget breakfast under 50 CZK (~€2).
meals.lunch: Kantýna (Politických vězňů 5, Nové Město) — a beloved local canteen with fresh Czech home-cooked meals. Daily specials (polední menu) cost ~150–200 CZK (~€6–8) including soup and main.
meals.dinner: Nusle or Vinohrady neighborhood local restaurant — try 'svíčková na smetaně' or 'řízek' (Czech schnitzel) at a neighborhood hospoda (pub). Budget ~200–300 CZK (~€8–12).

day_by_day.notes: Thursday is a great day to explore local neighborhoods away from the tourist crowds. Vinohrady has excellent coffee shops and wine bars if you want a relaxed evening. September weather in Prague is mild (15–20°C), so a light jacket is recommended for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at Letná Park (Letenské sady) — free entry, stunning panoramic views of Prague's red rooftops and the Vltava River from the giant metronome platform. A favorite spot for locals jogging and cycling. Completely free and underrated by tourists.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mucha Museum (Panská 7) dedicated to Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha — entry ~300 CZK (~€12). Afterward, explore the Josefov Jewish Quarter more thoroughly — visit the Old Jewish Cemetery and synagogues (combined ticket ~500 CZK, but deeply historically significant).
day_by_day.evening: Pack your bags and prepare for the overnight journey to Budapest. Take a budget FlixBus or RegioJet night bus from Prague Florenc bus station (~€15–25 booked in advance). Buses depart late evening and arrive in Budapest early morning, saving a night's accommodation cost.

meals.breakfast: Café Imperial (Na Poříčí 15) — a stunning Art Deco café for a special morning treat. Coffee and pastry ~150–200 CZK. Or a cheaper option: bakery near hotel for ~60 CZK.
meals.lunch: Nase Maso (Dlouhá 39, Old Town) — a local butcher-restaurant famous for Czech burgers and meat dishes. Lunch ~200–280 CZK (~€8–11). A true local favorite.
meals.dinner: Quick and budget-friendly dinner before departure — grab a 'párek v rohlíku' (Czech hot dog) or kebab near Florenc bus station for ~80–120 CZK (~€3–5). Save money for Budapest.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Prague–Budapest overnight bus well in advance on FlixBus or RegioJet for the cheapest fares. RegioJet is known for excellent comfort and free coffee/tea on board — highly recommended for budget travelers. Arrive at Florenc bus station at least 30 minutes early.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive in Budapest Népliget bus station early morning (~6:00–8:00 AM). Take Metro Line 3 to the city center. Check in to your Budapest accommodation (or store luggage if check-in isn't available yet). Head straight to the iconic Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) on the Danube bank — exterior views are free and breathtaking, especially in morning light. Book a guided interior tour in advance (~8,000 HUF / ~€20).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Belváros (Inner City) district — walk along the Danube Promenade, visit Vörösmarty Square, and stroll down Váci Street (the main pedestrian shopping street). Cross the iconic Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) on foot for free and explore the Buda Castle Hill area.
day_by_day.evening: Climb up to Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) on Castle Hill — free entry to the terraces in the evening (daytime has a small fee). Enjoy spectacular panoramic views of Pest, the Danube, and the Parliament at golden hour. Explore the historic Buda Castle neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Grab a 'lángos' (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese) from a street vendor near the bus station or city center — Budapest's most iconic street food, ~800–1,200 HUF (~€2–3).
meals.lunch: Főzelékfaló Ételbár (Akácfa u. 5, Pest) — a local canteen famous for 'főzelék' (Hungarian vegetable stew dishes). Hearty and authentic lunch for ~1,500–2,000 HUF (~€4–5).
meals.dinner: Menza Restaurant (Liszt Ferenc tér 2) — a retro-style Hungarian restaurant in the lively Liszt Ferenc Square. Try goulash soup and chicken paprikash. Budget ~3,000–4,500 HUF (~€8–12) per person.

day_by_day.notes: Budapest uses Hungarian Forint (HUF). As of 2027, approximate rate: €1 ≈ 380–400 HUF. Buy a 24-hour Budapest transport pass (~2,500 HUF) covering metro, trams, and buses. Saturday means Fisherman's Bastion and Castle Hill will be busy — go early evening for fewer crowds and better light.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Great Market Hall (Nagy Vásárcsarnok) — Budapest's largest and most spectacular indoor market, open Sunday mornings. Browse stalls selling paprika, sausages, embroidered tablecloths, and local produce. Try a 'kürtőskalács' (chimney cake) for ~800 HUF. Entry is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Jewish Quarter (VII District) — visit the stunning Dohány Street Synagogue (Dohány utcai zsinagóga), the largest synagogue in Europe. Entry ~5,000 HUF (~€13). Wander the ruin bar district (romkocsmák) — the famous Szimpla Kert opens for a Sunday farmers market in the afternoon (free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Experience Budapest's legendary ruin bar scene — Szimpla Kert (Kazinczy u. 14) is the original and most iconic ruin bar, set in a beautifully decaying old building. Enjoy affordable local craft beers (~700–1,000 HUF per beer) and live music in a truly unique atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the Great Market Hall — pick up fresh bread, local cheeses, and cold cuts from market stalls for a self-assembled breakfast under ~1,500 HUF (~€4).
meals.lunch: Bors GasztroBar (Kazinczy u. 10, Jewish Quarter) — a tiny, legendary Budapest street food spot famous for creative soups and baguette sandwiches. Lunch ~1,500–2,000 HUF (~€4–5). Expect a short queue — worth it.
meals.dinner: Karavan Street Food Court (Kazinczy u. 18, next to Szimpla) — an outdoor street food market with various vendors offering burgers, langos, BBQ ribs, and more. Dinner ~2,000–3,000 HUF (~€5–8). Perfect for a casual Sunday evening.

day_by_day.notes: Sunday is a wonderful day in Budapest's Jewish Quarter — the area comes alive with markets, cafés, and cultural energy. The Szimpla Sunday farmers market (10:00–14:00) is a beloved local tradition with organic produce, handmade crafts, and live music. Ruin bars get busier after 21:00.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) — a grand UNESCO-listed square with the Millennium Monument celebrating Hungarian history — completely free. Walk through the adjacent City Park (Városliget) and admire the fairy-tale Vajdahunyad Castle from the outside (free). September means the park is lush and green.
day_by_day.afternoon: Treat yourself to a traditional Hungarian thermal bath experience at Széchenyi Baths (Széchenyi fürdő) in City Park — one of Europe's largest and most beautiful bath complexes. Entry ~7,000–9,000 HUF (~€18–23) for a day ticket. A quintessential Budapest experience and genuinely relaxing after days of walking.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Danube Embankment at night — visit the haunting 'Shoes on the Danube Bank' memorial (free) commemorating WWII victims. The illuminated Parliament Building and Chain Bridge at night are among Europe's most beautiful urban views.

meals.breakfast: Auguszt Cukrászda (Kossuth Lajos u. 14) — a historic Budapest pastry shop. Try a 'rétes' (Hungarian strudel) and coffee for ~1,000–1,500 HUF (~€3–4).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for City Park — buy fresh bread, salami, paprika cheese, and fruit from a local 'ABC' supermarket (Spar or Lidl) for ~1,500–2,000 HUF total. Eat by the lake near Vajdahunyad Castle.
meals.dinner: Frici Papa Kifőzdéje (Király u. 55, VII District) — a legendary, no-frills Hungarian 'kifőzde' (home-cooking restaurant) beloved by locals. Massive portions of goulash, stuffed cabbage, and liver dishes for ~2,000–3,000 HUF (~€5–8). Cash only, arrive early as it fills up fast.

day_by_day.notes: Széchenyi Baths are busiest on weekends — Monday is a great day to visit with fewer crowds. Bring a towel and flip-flops (or rent them there for extra cost). Lockers are included in the entry fee. The outdoor pools are heated to 38°C year-round, perfect for September evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — visit Gellért Hill (Gellért-hegy) for the best panoramic view of all Budapest. The hike up is free and takes about 20–30 minutes. Visit the Citadella fortress at the top (free exterior) and the Liberty Statue. On a clear September morning, you can see the entire city laid out before you.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute exploration of the Buda side — visit the historic Tabán neighborhood and the charming Krisztinaváros district. Browse local souvenir shops for affordable Hungarian paprika, Tokaj wine, and Unicum liqueur as gifts. Head back to your accommodation, collect luggage, and make your way to Budapest Keleti (Eastern) railway station or Liszt Ferenc Airport for your onward journey.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Budapest. If your flight/train is late evening, spend a final hour at a café on Liszt Ferenc Square (Gozsdu Udvar courtyard is beautiful) with a farewell 'fröccs' (Hungarian wine spritzer, ~600–800 HUF) and reflect on an incredible 8-day journey.

meals.breakfast: New York Café (Erzsébet krt. 9–11) — splurge slightly on your last morning at one of the world's most beautiful cafés for a coffee and pastry (~2,500–3,500 HUF). Or budget option: grab a fresh 'pogácsa' (savory scone) from a bakery for ~400 HUF.
meals.lunch: Hummus Bar (Alkotmány u. 20 or multiple locations) — a popular Budapest chain offering generous Middle Eastern-inspired plates. Excellent value at ~1,800–2,500 HUF (~€5–7). Great vegetarian options.
meals.dinner: Airport or departure meal — grab a final 'lángos' or chimney cake from a street vendor near Keleti station as a farewell snack. Budget ~800–1,200 HUF (~€2–3).

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 90 minutes to reach Budapest Liszt Ferenc Airport from the city center by public transport (Bus 100E from Deák Ferenc tér, ~900 HUF one way). For Keleti train station, most central accommodations are within 20–30 minutes by metro. Do a final currency exchange or spend remaining HUF before departure as it's difficult to exchange outside Hungary.

trip_options.title: Classic Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Time to clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to your boutique hotel in Staré Město (Old Town). Take the Airport Express bus or a mid-range taxi (~30–40 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely first walk through Staré Město. Stroll across Charles Bridge (Karlův most) to absorb the Gothic towers and baroque statues. Continue into the Lesser Town (Malá Strana) briefly before returning across the bridge at golden hour. No need to rush — let the city reveal itself organically.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Old Town Square at dusk: watch the famous Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime, admire the illuminated Church of Our Lady before Týn, and soak in the medieval atmosphere. End the evening with a relaxed walk along the Vltava riverbank.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick but authentic bite near the airport or upon arrival — try a local bakery (pekárna) near your hotel for an open-faced chlebíček sandwich and a coffee (~€5–8)
meals.dinner: Lokál Dlouhááá (Dlouhá 33, Staré Město) — a beloved Czech gastropub serving classic svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce), fresh Pilsner Urquell tank beer, and hearty soups. Mid-range, very local (~€15–22/person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Jet lag and travel fatigue are real — resist the urge to over-schedule. Pick up a Prague transit map and a city card brochure at the hotel front desk.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning at Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) — the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Arrive early (~9:00) to beat crowds. Visit St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička). Purchase a mid-range Circuit B ticket (~€12) covering the key highlights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through the charming Nerudova Street back into Malá Strana. Visit the ornate St. Nicholas Church (free entry to exterior, small fee inside). Cross back over Charles Bridge and explore the Josefov Jewish Quarter — walk through the historic synagogues and the Old Jewish Cemetery (combined ticket ~€18). A deeply moving and culturally rich experience.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Vinohrady or Žižkov neighborhood (15-min tram ride) for a more local evening away from tourist crowds. Explore the eclectic architecture and lively café culture.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or nearby café — try Café Louvre-style pastries and coffee at a Staré Město bakery (~€6–9)
meals.lunch: Malostranská beseda (Malostranské nám. 21) — a historic venue in Malá Strana with Czech classics like goulash and roast duck. Lovely courtyard seating (~€12–18/person)
meals.dinner: Eska (Pernerova 49, Karlín district) — a celebrated modern Czech restaurant using local, seasonal ingredients with a wood-fired oven. Slightly elevated but well within mid-range (~€20–28/person). Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Prague Castle involves significant uphill walking on cobblestones. September weather in Prague is typically mild (15–20°C), so a light layer is advisable for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mucha Museum (Panská 7) dedicated to Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha — compact, fascinating, and very manageable in 1.5 hours (~€12 entry). Afterward, walk to Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí), the historic heart of modern Prague, and reflect on its role in the 1968 Prague Spring and 1989 Velvet Revolution.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Nové Město (New Town) area: visit the National Museum at the top of Wenceslas Square (recently renovated, ~€10 entry) for Czech history and natural history exhibits. Then wander down to the Naplavka riverside farmers' market (active on weekends but the embankment is lovely any day) for a relaxed riverside stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert — Prague is famous for affordable, high-quality performances. Check listings at the Estates Theatre (Stavovské divadlo, where Mozart premiered Don Giovanni) or Municipal House (Obecní dům). Tickets typically €15–35 for mid-range seats.

meals.breakfast: Café Savoy (Vítězná 5, Malá Strana) — a beautifully restored Art Nouveau café with exceptional pastries, eggs, and coffee. A Prague institution (~€10–14/person)
meals.lunch: Nase Maso (Dlouhá 39) — a butcher-deli hybrid beloved by locals. Order a beef tartare or roast pork sandwich at the counter. Casual, cheap, and absolutely delicious (~€8–12/person)
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Café Imperial (Na Příkopě 15) — a stunning tiled Art Deco restaurant serving elevated Czech and Central European cuisine. Great atmosphere (~€20–28/person)

day_by_day.notes: Book concert tickets online in advance — September is peak cultural season in Prague and good seats sell out. The Estates Theatre is especially atmospheric and historically significant.

day_by_day.morning: Half-day trip to Vyšehrad Fortress (30-min walk or short tram ride from Old Town). This lesser-visited hilltop citadel offers stunning panoramic views of Prague and the Vltava, the ancient Rotunda of St. Martin, and the Vyšehrad Cemetery where Dvořák and Smetana are buried. Far fewer tourists than Prague Castle — a hidden gem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city center and visit the Franz Kafka Museum (Cihelná 2b, Malá Strana) — an immersive, atmospheric exhibition on the life and work of Prague's most famous literary son (~€10 entry). Browse the antique bookshops and design stores along Malá Strana's side streets afterward.
day_by_day.evening: Last evening in Prague — explore the Žižkov neighborhood's legendary pub culture. Visit one of the local pivnice (beer halls) for a final Czech pivo. The TV Tower (Žižkovský vysílač) is open late and offers a spectacular night view of the city from its observation deck (~€8).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick stop at a local pekárna for a croissant and espresso
meals.lunch: Picnic at Vyšehrad — grab supplies from a local deli or supermarket near Nové Město (cold cuts, local cheese, Czech bread, and a beer). Eat with a view of the Vltava. (~€6–10/person)
meals.dinner: Pivnice u Rudolfina (Křížovnická 10) — a cozy traditional Czech pub near the Old Town with excellent pork knuckle (vepřové koleno), dumplings, and sauerkraut. Very local, very satisfying (~€12–18/person)

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight — tomorrow you travel to Budapest. Check train or bus schedules in advance. The RegioJet or FlixBus overnight/morning routes from Prague to Budapest are comfortable and budget-friendly (book online, ~€20–40). Alternatively, a direct train takes ~6–7 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Morning departure from Prague to Budapest by train or bus. The journey takes approximately 6–7 hours by train (Praha hl.n. to Budapest-Keleti). Enjoy the Central European countryside rolling past — pack snacks or grab food from the station. Arrive in Budapest early-to-mid afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your Budapest accommodation (ideally in the Belváros/District V or District VII areas for central access). Take a first orientation walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side — absorb the iconic panorama of Buda Castle, the Chain Bridge, and the Parliament building across the water. Visit the majestic Hungarian Parliament Building exterior (book a tour in advance if desired, ~€20).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Ruin Bar (romkocsma) scene in the Jewish Quarter (District VII). Szimpla Kert (Kazinczy u. 14) is the original and most famous ruin bar — a sprawling, eclectic space in a crumbling courtyard filled with local art, mismatched furniture, and live music. Perfect for a first Budapest evening.

meals.breakfast: Train station café or packed snacks from Prague for the journey
meals.lunch: On the train — bring Czech provisions or purchase from the dining car
meals.dinner: Frici Papa Kifőzdéje (Király u. 55, District VII) — a legendary Hungarian home-cooking restaurant (kifőzde) beloved by locals. Try gulyás (goulash), pörkölt (meat stew), and lángos (fried dough). Incredibly affordable and authentic (~€8–12/person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Budapest accommodation in advance — September is high season and the city is very popular. The District V (Belváros) or District VII (Erzsébetváros/Jewish Quarter) locations offer the best central access on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Cross the Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) on foot to the Buda side. Climb Castle Hill via the funicular (Budavári Sikló, ~€5) or the scenic stairway. Explore Buda Castle (Budavári Palota), the Hungarian National Gallery (free on Sundays for EU citizens, otherwise ~€8), and the cobblestone streets of the Castle District. Visit the Matthias Church and the Fisherman's Bastion for breathtaking panoramic views over Pest and the Danube.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the Gellért Hill area and visit the Gellért Thermal Baths (Kelenhegyi út 4) — a stunning Art Nouveau spa complex. Spend 2–3 hours soaking in the thermal pools, steam rooms, and outdoor wave pool. Entry ~€20–25 (mid-range, includes locker). A quintessential Budapest experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Pest for the evening. Walk along Andrássy Avenue (Budapest's Champs-Élysées, a UNESCO World Heritage street) toward Heroes' Square (Hősök tere). As dusk falls, the illuminated monuments are spectacular. Return via the M1 metro (the oldest underground railway in continental Europe).

meals.breakfast: New York Café (Erzsébet krt. 9–11) — the most beautiful café in Budapest, often called the most beautiful in the world. Splurge slightly on coffee and pastries in this gilded, frescoed hall (~€12–16/person). Worth every forint.
meals.lunch: Borkonyha Winekitchen (Sas u. 3, District V) — a Michelin Bib Gourmand Hungarian bistro with seasonal menus and excellent local wines. Mid-range lunch menu (~€18–25/person). Book ahead.
meals.dinner: Kiosk Budapest (március 15. tér 4) — a stylish riverside restaurant with Hungarian and Mediterranean dishes, great Danube views, and a lively Sunday atmosphere (~€18–25/person)

day_by_day.notes: Bring a swimsuit and a small towel (or rent one at Gellért Baths). Sunday is a popular day at the baths — arrive early (before 11:00) or after 15:00 to avoid peak crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai zsinagóga) — the largest synagogue in Europe and the second largest in the world. The complex includes the Jewish Museum, the Raoul Wallenberg Memorial Garden, and the haunting Holocaust Memorial Tree of Life. A profoundly important cultural and historical site (~€15 entry). Afterward, walk through the Jewish Quarter's vibrant street art and café culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Central Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok, Fővám tér 1–3) — Budapest's magnificent 19th-century iron-and-brick market. Browse stalls of Hungarian paprika, salami, Tokaji wine, foie gras, and handmade crafts on the ground floor. The upper gallery has lángos stalls and folk art vendors. Perfect for souvenir shopping and snacking. Then walk along the Pest riverbank toward the moving Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on the Danube — take a 1-hour evening river cruise to see Budapest's illuminated skyline from the water. Parliament, Buda Castle, and the bridges lit up at night are truly unforgettable. Several operators run mid-range cruises (~€15–25, some include a drink).

meals.breakfast: Café Gerbeaud (Vörösmarty tér 7) — a historic grand café on Vörösmarty Square. Order Gerbeaud cake (a walnut-and-apricot layered pastry) and a strong Hungarian coffee (~€10–14/person)
meals.lunch: Street food lunch at the Central Market Hall upper floor — lángos with sour cream and cheese, kürtőskalács (chimney cake), and fresh-pressed juice (~€6–10/person)
meals.dinner: Costes Downtown (Vigyázó Ferenc u. 5) — a Michelin-starred restaurant offering a refined Hungarian tasting menu. A special splurge dinner to mark your penultimate evening. Tasting menu ~€55–75/person (reserve well in advance)

day_by_day.notes: The Danube cruise is best booked online same-day or the day before in September. Carry some Hungarian Forints (HUF) for market purchases — not all stalls accept cards. The Shoes on the Danube memorial is open 24/7 and free.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Széchenyi Thermal Baths (Állatkerti krt. 9–11, City Park) — the grandest of Budapest's thermal bath complexes, housed in a stunning yellow Neo-Baroque palace. Soak in the famous outdoor chess-player pools and indoor thermal halls. Arrive early (~8:00) to enjoy the misty morning atmosphere before crowds arrive (~€22–28 entry with locker).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore City Park (Városliget) adjacent to the baths — visit Vajdahunyad Castle (free entry to grounds, a romantic Gothic-Renaissance-Baroque fantasy built for the 1896 millennium exhibition) and the Museum of Fine Arts if time allows (~€8 entry). Stroll back down Andrássy Avenue for any last-minute shopping or café stops.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Budapest — return to the Belváros for a farewell dinner and a leisurely walk across the illuminated Chain Bridge one last time. Reflect on eight remarkable days across two extraordinary Central European capitals.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at a local café near your hotel — pastry, yogurt, and coffee (~€6–8)
meals.lunch: Belvárosi Lugas Étterem (Bajcsy-Zsilinszky út 15) — a cozy, unpretentious Hungarian restaurant popular with locals. Try chicken paprikash (csirkepaprikás) with nokedli (egg dumplings) and a glass of Egri Bikavér (Bull's Blood red wine) (~€12–16/person)
meals.dinner: Stand25 Bisztró (Nagyvárad tér 2) — a critically acclaimed modern Hungarian bistro known for its creative takes on classic dishes. Relaxed, stylish, and delicious. (~€22–30/person). A perfect farewell meal.

day_by_day.notes: If your departure flight is early on Day 9, pack bags tonight and arrange an airport transfer in advance. Budapest Liszt Ferenc Airport is ~30 min from the city center by taxi or the 100E airport express bus (~€3). Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for check-in and security.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Václav Havel Airport to boutique hotel in Staré Město (Old Town). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your premium accommodations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through Staré Město. Stroll across the iconic Charles Bridge, admire the 30 Baroque statues, and soak in panoramic views of the Vltava River. Continue to Old Town Square to see the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and the twin-spired Týn Church. Explore the winding medieval lanes at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on a rooftop terrace overlooking the red rooftops of Prague's Old Town. Afterward, a leisurely first dinner at a top-tier Czech restaurant to ease into the city.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport lounge)
meals.lunch: Light welcome meal at Café Savoy — a beautifully restored Neo-Renaissance café near the river, known for its vaulted ceilings and refined Czech pastries and soups.
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise — a Michelin-starred restaurant in Old Town offering a multi-course tasting menu rooted in historic Czech recipes, paired with exceptional Czech and European wines.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Confirm hotel concierge for next-day reservations. September in Prague is mild (15–22°C), ideal for walking. Pack a light jacket for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex (Pražský hrad) visit — the largest ancient castle in the world. Explore St. Vitus Cathedral with its stunning Gothic stained glass, the Old Royal Palace, the Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička), and panoramic city views from the castle ramparts. Hire a private licensed guide for an immersive 2.5-hour experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) — Prague's baroque quarter. Visit the ornate St. Nicholas Church, browse antique shops and art galleries along Nerudova Street. Cross back over Charles Bridge and explore Josefov, Prague's historic Jewish Quarter. Tour the Old Jewish Cemetery, the Pinkas Synagogue (Holocaust memorial), and the Spanish Synagogue.
day_by_day.evening: Classical music concert at the Rudolfinum or Municipal House (Obecní dům) — both world-class venues hosting the Prague Philharmonic or chamber ensembles. Pre-concert champagne in the ornate lobby.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or Café Imperial — a stunning Art Nouveau café with mosaic-tiled walls, offering a lavish breakfast spread with eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, and Czech pastries.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch from Naše Maso butcher deli (premium charcuterie, local cheeses, artisan bread) enjoyed in the castle gardens or along the Vltava embankment.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Field Restaurant — a Michelin-starred, farm-to-table fine dining experience in Old Town, with creative contemporary Czech cuisine and an outstanding natural wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Book private castle guide in advance through hotel concierge. Concert tickets should be reserved ahead — September is peak cultural season. Comfortable walking shoes essential for cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Prague National Gallery at the Schwarzenberg Palace and Sternberg Palace — housing Bohemian Gothic art, Baroque masterpieces, and European Old Masters. Followed by a private walking tour of Hradčany (Castle District) neighborhood, exploring hidden courtyards and noble palaces rarely seen by tourists.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon at leisure in Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods — Prague's elegant residential districts. Browse independent bookshops, design boutiques, and local galleries. Visit the striking Žižkov Television Tower with its iconic crawling baby sculptures and panoramic views from the top-floor observation deck.
day_by_day.evening: Prague's craft cocktail and jazz scene — visit Hemingway Bar, one of Central Europe's finest cocktail bars, known for its 1920s Parisian atmosphere and expertly crafted classic cocktails. Then dinner in a historic wine cellar.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at Eska — a celebrated modern Czech restaurant in the Žižkov area, with a wood-fired kitchen, sourdough baked in-house, and seasonal menus sourced from local farms.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lokál Dlouhááá — a beloved upscale Czech gastropub in Old Town, serving perfectly poured Pilsner Urquell tank beer and elevated traditional dishes like svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) and roast duck.

day_by_day.notes: Vinohrady is about 20 minutes by tram from Old Town — a great way to experience local Prague life. Consider a private driver for the evening to move between venues comfortably.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kutná Hora (1 hour from Prague by private car) — a UNESCO World Heritage town. Visit the extraordinary Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church), decorated with the bones of 40,000 people, and the magnificent Gothic Cathedral of Saint Barbara, one of the finest Gothic churches in Central Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Prague. Afternoon spa and wellness session at your hotel or at the luxury August spa — enjoy a traditional Czech herbal treatment, hot stone massage, or thermal bath ritual to recharge before the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Prague at one of the city's most iconic settings, followed by a private night walk along the illuminated Charles Bridge and Old Town Square — magical when tourist crowds thin out.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast (early, before departure to Kutná Hora)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Dacický Restaurant in Kutná Hora — a historic restaurant in a 16th-century building serving traditional Bohemian cuisine, local game, and Moravian wines.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Alcron Restaurant (Radisson Blu Alcron Hotel) — an Art Deco masterpiece with Michelin recognition, offering a refined seafood-focused tasting menu with exceptional sommelier service.

day_by_day.notes: Private car to Kutná Hora is strongly recommended over train for comfort and flexibility. Kutná Hora visit takes approximately 4–5 hours. Book spa treatments in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer from Prague to Budapest by premium car or first-class train (Budapest Keleti station, approximately 7 hours by train or 5 hours by car). The scenic route passes through the Bohemian and Moravian countryside. Alternatively, a short 1-hour flight is available for those preferring speed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrival in Budapest. Check into luxury hotel in the city center (Buda Castle district or Andrássy Avenue area). First impressions walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) — admiring the iconic Chain Bridge, the Hungarian Parliament Building across the river, and the Buda Castle hill silhouette.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Ruin Bar scene of the Jewish Quarter — begin with cocktails at Szimpla Kert, Budapest's most famous ruin bar, set inside a crumbling 19th-century building filled with eclectic art and live music. Then transition to a refined dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast in Prague before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic or dining car on the train, or a stop at a countryside restaurant en route if traveling by private car.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Costes Downtown — Budapest's first Michelin-starred restaurant, offering inventive Hungarian-inspired cuisine with a world-class wine list, located in the heart of Pest.

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets (first class) or private transfer well in advance — this is a popular route. If flying, schedule a late morning flight to maximize Prague morning time. September is Budapest's golden season — warm, sunny, and festive.

day_by_day.morning: Buda Castle Hill exploration — take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló) up to Buda Castle, home to the Hungarian National Gallery and Budapest History Museum. Walk through the medieval Castle District, visit Matthias Church with its dazzling Zsolnay tile roof, and admire the Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) with its fairy-tale turrets and sweeping panoramic views over the Danube and Pest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Chain Bridge on foot to Pest. Visit the extraordinary Hungarian Parliament Building (exterior and optional guided interior tour — one of the world's most beautiful parliament buildings). Stroll along Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's Champs-Élysées — lined with Neo-Renaissance mansions, luxury boutiques, and the State Opera House. Visit the Hungarian State Opera House for a guided interior tour.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a world-class opera or ballet performance at the Hungarian State Opera House — one of the most beautiful opera houses in Europe, with lavish gilded interiors. Pre-performance dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at New York Café — arguably the most beautiful café in the world, a 19th-century Neo-Baroque masterpiece with frescoed ceilings, gold leaf columns, and an opulent breakfast menu.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Borkonyha Winekitchen — a Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant near the Parliament, known for its outstanding Hungarian wine pairings and refined seasonal cuisine.
meals.dinner: Pre-opera dinner at Onyx Restaurant — a two Michelin-starred restaurant on Vörösmarty Square, offering a sophisticated tasting menu celebrating Hungarian culinary heritage with avant-garde techniques.

day_by_day.notes: Opera tickets must be booked well in advance — Sunday performances sell out quickly. Smart dress code required for the Opera House. The Fisherman's Bastion is most spectacular at sunrise or late afternoon light.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury thermal spa morning at Széchenyi Thermal Bath — Budapest's grandest Neo-Baroque bathhouse, built in 1913. Book a private cabin and enjoy the thermal pools, steam rooms, and optional massage treatments. This is a quintessential Budapest experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — Budapest's largest and most beautiful covered market, with ornate Zsolnay tile roof. Browse stalls of Hungarian paprika, foie gras, Tokaji wine, artisan salami, embroidered textiles, and handmade crafts. Followed by a private food tour of the Jewish Quarter (Erzsébetváros) — sampling lángos, chimney cake (kürtőskalács), Jewish-style stuffed cabbage, and Hungarian street food.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Danube River cruise on a private luxury boat — champagne and canapés while floating past illuminated landmarks: the Parliament, Chain Bridge, Buda Castle, and Gellért Hill. One of the most spectacular urban views in Europe at night.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at Gerbeaud — Budapest's most iconic café and confectionery on Vörösmarty Square, established in 1858. Try the Dobos torte, Esterházy cake, and Hungarian goulash soup.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Stand Restaurant — a Michelin-starred chef's table experience by Tamás Széll, celebrating modern Hungarian cuisine with bold flavors, local ingredients, and theatrical presentation.

day_by_day.notes: Book Széchenyi private cabin and massage in advance. The private Danube cruise should be arranged through hotel concierge — typically 1.5–2 hours. Bring a light layer for the evening on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit the Dohány Street Synagogue (Great Synagogue), the largest synagogue in Europe and a hauntingly beautiful memorial to Budapest's Jewish heritage. Explore the adjacent Jewish Museum and the Holocaust Memorial (Weeping Willow Tree). Then browse the elegant boutiques and galleries of the Váci Street and Falk Miksa Street antiques district for last-minute luxury souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely farewell lunch and final stroll along the Danube Promenade. Visit the iconic Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial — a deeply moving Holocaust memorial of 60 iron shoes cast along the riverbank. Depending on departure time, relax at the hotel spa or enjoy a final coffee at a historic café.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport for departure. End of an extraordinary 8-day premium journey through the heart of Central Europe.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at Café Gerbeaud or in-hotel — indulge in a final Hungarian breakfast with fresh pastries, cold cuts, local honey, and strong espresso.
meals.lunch: Final lunch at Spoon The Boat — a floating restaurant moored on the Danube, offering refined international and Hungarian cuisine with unbeatable views of the Chain Bridge and Buda Castle.
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or early dinner at the hotel before transfer — alternatively, a light farewell dinner at 360 Bar rooftop on the Opera House for a final panoramic view of Budapest at dusk.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure from Budapest Airport. Consider purchasing Tokaji Aszú wine, Hungarian paprika, Unicum herbal liqueur, and Zsolnay porcelain as premium gifts. Ensure hotel checkout is arranged with luggage storage if flight departs late.
